references.text: Jacob deliberately places his right hand on Ephraim's head and his left on Manasseh, even though Manasseh is the firstborn – this is the action Joseph reacts to in verse 17.
Jacob explains why he prefers Ephraim over Manasseh and blesses them, as a direct response to Joseph's objection in verse 17.
Isaac blesses Jacob over Esau, a parallel to how Jacob chooses the younger (Ephraim) over the older (Manasseh), in line with God's pattern of choosing the younger.
Jacob's blessing of Joseph, continuing the special position Joseph and his sons received, connected to the events in chapter 48.
The tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh receive their land inheritance in Canaan, reflecting Jacob's blessing and the preferred position given to Ephraim.
Hebrews 11:21 mentions Jacob's faith when he blessed each of Joseph's sons, a direct reference to the blessing action in Genesis 48.
Continues the same event; 48:1 introduces the brothers who become the subject of the conflict in 48:17.
Same sequence of events; 46:29 is the reunion that leads directly to the blessing in 48:17.
Confirms the identity of the two brothers; 48:17 shows the action, Numbers 26:28 establishes the family structure.
Causality between the blessing and land distribution; 48:17 explains why Ephraim receives the leading position in Joshua.
Temporal connection; 48:17 is the action to secure the future, 50:23 shows the fulfillment in the third generation.
